demo_doc_001: Oskeria is an island nation in the Gulf of Amberly. Velmaran, the capital of Oskeria, sits on the northern coast and has been the seat of the Oskerian assembly since 1802. Port Ilse, the second city, lies at the mouth of the Ardune.
demo_doc_002: The Ardune rises in the Morrowfen hills and runs through Velmaran before reaching the sea at Port Ilse. Its quays in Velmaran were rebuilt after the flood of 1911.
demo_doc_003: The Selm rises on the slopes of Mount Corran and runs through the market town of Hadley before joining the Ardune below Port Ilse. It does not pass through Velmaran.
demo_doc_004: The Varrow rises in the Morrowfen hills, east of the Ardune's source, and flows south through the Brannoch marshes to the Gulf of Amberly.
demo_doc_005: Rivers of Oskeria. The island has three rivers longer than twenty kilometres: the Ardune, the Selm and the Varrow. Smaller streams are not listed here.
demo_doc_006: Lanterns of Morrowfen, an opera in three acts, was composed by Ilsa Renvaar and first staged in Velmaran in 1868.
demo_doc_007: Ilsa Renvaar founded the Velmaran Conservatory in 1874 and directed it until her death in 1901.
demo_doc_008: A guide to the conservatories of Oskeria lists the Velmaran Conservatory among the oldest, without naming its founder. The Port Ilse Conservatory was founded in 1880 by Davin Kesh.
demo_doc_009: Tomas Hale kept the lighthouse at Cape Vardequist from 1890 to 1921 and logged every ship that rounded the cape.
demo_doc_010: The first atlas of the Oskerian coast, published in 1904, was compiled by a committee of the Velmaran Geographical Society.
demo_doc_011: Velmaran travel notes: walk along the Ardune quays, visit the conservatory founded by Ilsa Renvaar, and take the ferry to Port Ilse.
demo_doc_012: The Morrowfen hills are a range of low uplands in central Oskeria. Two rivers rise there, the Ardune and the Varrow; the Selm rises further west on Mount Corran.
demo_doc_013: Edda Morlan succeeded Tomas Hale as keeper of the Cape Vardequist lighthouse in 1921 and, like him, logged every ship that rounded the cape until she retired in 1940.
demo_doc_014: After Ilsa Renvaar's death in 1901, the composer Oren Vasse directed the Velmaran Conservatory until 1930.

demo_doc_103: The Velmaran Conservatory: a short history. The Velmaran Conservatory was founded in 1874 by the composer Ilsa Renvaar, whose opera Lanterns of Morrowfen had been staged in the city six years earlier. Renvaar directed the conservatory until her death in 1901. Under her direction it trained the first generation of Oskerian orchestral players, and its concert hall on the Ardune quays opened in 1889. The conservatory moved to its present building on Assembly Square in 1932, after the old hall was damaged by fire. Today it teaches composition, voice and every orchestral instrument, and its library holds the manuscripts of Renvaar and of her pupils, among them the scores of three operas and more than forty songs. Visitors may attend the open rehearsals held on Thursday evenings during term.

demo_doc_105: Port Ilse, the second city of Oskeria, lies at the mouth of the Ardune. The Port Ilse Conservatory was founded in 1880 by Davin Kesh, a cellist from Hadley. The fish market of Port Ilse is the largest on the Gulf of Amberly.
demo_doc_106: The Renvaar Prize for young composers, named after Ilsa Renvaar, has been awarded by the Velmaran Conservatory every year since 1950.
